result.title: Beyond Scene Shortcuts: Action-Centric Video-Text Alignment for Fine-Grained Action Understanding
result.summary: Fine-grained action understanding requires vision-language models to ground what an agent does, how it acts, and why it acts in spatio-temporal evidence. However, richer supervision can backfire: fine-tuned models may generate detailed action descriptions grounded in static scenes and salient objects rather than motion, a failure we call Environment-Grounded Action Hallucination (EGAH). To mitigate EGAH, we propose Staged Attention Rectification and Reinforcement (STARR), an action-centric video-text alignment framework that breaks scene-action shortcuts through Action-Environment Dissociation and reinforces action-focused grounding with an Attention Consistency Reward within Group Relative Policy Optimization. We further construct FineActionR&R, combining temporally localized captions with hierarchical and temporal-causal reasoning data. Built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, FineActionVLM-R1 improves average MotionBench accuracy by 3.01 percentage points over its base model and achieves 91.50% on HAU-MCQ-Bench. Qualitative comparisons further indicate more faithful fine-grained action descriptions with fewer environment-induced hallucinations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断视频 VLM 在细粒度动作理解中依赖静态场景与显著物体的「环境锚定动作幻觉」，并提出 STARR 训练框架，以动作—环境解离和注意力一致性奖励强化动作聚焦的时空证据对齐。
AI.relevance_reason: 其环境捷径诊断与注意力一致性约束可为 LVR 中视觉旁路、证据筛选和内部状态是否真正编码动作信息提供核查线索；但方法主要在输出与训练层面干预，尚需确认是否触及 latent 推理状态。
